business_problem: Mitsubishi Research Institute DCS needed to improve proposal quality and development speed because competitive IT-consulting work required faster customer-tailored recommendations and more efficient code generation.
solution_summary: Mitsubishi Research Institute DCS ran a three-month proof of concept with IBM watsonx.ai to address two related bottlenecks: proposal development and code generation. For consulting support, IBM Client Engineering helped build a solution that analyzes meeting transcripts, quantifies participant excitement and interest, and combines those signals with related metrics such as speaking time so the firm can draft more compelling proposals. In parallel, the teams applied the same generative AI platform to software-delivery work by validating and generating code from existing design documents while honoring internal development rules. IBM also built an Eclipse IDE extension that lets engineers invoke code generation directly from their working environment through an API. This architecture turns transcripts and design artifacts into structured AI inputs, then routes the resulting recommendations and code back into consulting and engineering workflows so teams can pursue more business with less manual effort.

solution_components.role: Analyzes transcripts for proposal intelligence and generates code from design documents for development workflows.

solution_components.name: IBM Client Engineering
solution_components.role: Co-developed the proof of concept and validated how generative AI could be embedded into consulting and coding work.
